source._otp_source_note: OTP 28.5.0.8 (released 2026-10-14) and Elixir 1.20.4 are the newest 28.x / 1.20.x releases on 2026-10-22. sha256s: OTP = the GitHub release asset digest, equal to the release's SHA256.txt and to the official erlang:28 image's OTP_DOWNLOAD_SHA256; Elixir = the v1.20.4 source archive, equal to the official elixir:1.20 image's ELIXIR_DOWNLOAD_SHA256 (both checked 2026-10-22; the archive re-downloaded). configure_flags keep the OTP application set of erlang:28-slim, which r1 ran on, minus odbc and SCTP (their libraries are not installed and RabbitMQ uses neither) and the Java/wx GUI parts. To move to a newer OTP patch: update version/url/sha256 here (the renderer refuses a version that disagrees with otp_version, or a short sha256).
source._toolchain_note: RabbitMQ 4.4.x CI (test-make.yaml, v4.4.0) builds + tests against OTP {27,28,29} x Elixir 1.20; deps/rabbitmq_cli/mix.exs accepts Elixir >= 1.17 and < 1.21. We pick OTP 28 + Elixir 1.20: the Elixir upstream tests 4.4 with, and the OTP series 4.3.6-r1 already ran on (RabbitMQ's 4.4.0 notes advise against moving RabbitMQ to 4.4 and Erlang to a new series in one step; this release keeps the series). Since 2026-10-10 the image is Ubuntu 24.04: no official Erlang or Elixir image is built on Ubuntu, and noble's own packages are erlang 25.3 and elixir 1.14, below RabbitMQ 4.3's minimum, so the offline build compiles Erlang/OTP and Elixir from source (source.otp_source / elixir_source) on the pinned ubuntu:24.04 -- the recipe the official erlang and elixir images use on Debian (./configure && make && make install; Elixir `make install`) -- and OTP's crypto NIF links Ubuntu's libssl3t64. Elixir goes to /opt/elixir and stays in the build stage. The online vendor stage still uses the official elixir:1.20-otp-28-slim (Debian 13): `make source-dist` only fetches and bundles source. rabbitmq-components.mk sets ELIXIR=system, so the build stage's mix/elixirc (on PATH) is used. The official docker-library rabbitmq image is also ubuntu:24.04 with OTP compiled from source.
source._build_packages_note: Erlang/OTP + Elixir + erlc/escript are compiled in the offline otpbuild stage from source; that build needs build-essential (gcc/g++ for erts and the JIT, make), perl (OTP's build scripts), libssl-dev (the crypto NIF, linked to Ubuntu's libssl3t64), libncurses-dev (erts termcap, libtinfo6) and zlib1g-dev (erts zlib). The rest is the host toolchain erlang.mk/the packaging Makefile invoke: make (build-essential->gcc/make), git (erlang.mk fetches deps + does git-describe versioning), zip/unzip + xz-utils (source-dist + generic-unix tarball pack/unpack), rsync (source-dist file assembly), xsltproc (the generic-unix `manpages`/`web-manpages` targets render docbook man pages -- omitting it breaks `make package-generic-unix`), python3 (a couple of plugin codegen scripts). ca-certificates for the git/https dep fetch in the ONLINE vendor stage only. The same list is installed in the online vendor stage (elixir:1.20-otp-28-slim, Debian 13) and vendored as build debs from the pinned ubuntu:24.04; every name exists on both (checked 2026-10-10).
vendor_outputs: deps/  (every erlang.mk dependency fetched in-tree -- the vendored dep set)
PACKAGES/rabbitmq-server-4.4.1.tar.xz  (self-contained source-dist tarball; all deps bundled)

install._note: Mirrors packaging/docker-image/Dockerfile: extract the generic-unix release to /opt/rabbitmq --strip-components 1, then force SYS_PREFIX= empty so the broker reads config from /etc/rabbitmq (not /opt/rabbitmq/etc). PATH must include /opt/rabbitmq/sbin (rabbitmq-server, rabbitmqctl, rabbitmq-diagnostics, rabbitmq-plugins).

source._offline_vendor_note: HERMETIC/OFFLINE VENDOR GAP (highest risk): erlang.mk fetches deps via git during `make`. The ONLINE `make source-dist` must populate deps/ with EVERY dep (and bundle them into the source-dist tarball) so the OFFLINE `make package-generic-unix` recompiles with --network=none. erlang.mk will NOT refetch a dep that is already present in deps/, but the kit MUST ship the populated deps/ tree (not just the tarball) and may need IGNORE_DEPS / DEPS_DIR set so no git is attempted offline. This is the source-rebuild-erlang analog of the etcd per-module `go mod vendor` gap -- prove the --network=none build before certifying.
